channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Alberta Voters Reject Separation From Canada as Carney Triumphs
item.description: Voters in Alberta are set to reject separation from Canada, a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney after a long referendum campaign that created divisions in the country’s energy heartland.
item.dc:creator: Iain Boekhoff

item.title: Australia to Sue Social Media Firms on Alleged Breaches
item.description: Australia’s government is set to sue Facebook, TikTok and other major digital platforms for alleged non-compliance with a nationwide social media ban for under-16s, Communications Minister Anika Wells said. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Malaysia Will Form Special Body to Probe ‘Corporate Mafia’
item.description: Malaysia will establish a special committee to investigate allegations that a network of businessmen colluded with anti-graft agency officials to oust company executives, and that body will publish a report within three months, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
item.dc:creator: Niluksi Koswanage and Tom Redmond

item.title: Romania Set For New Premier to End Months of Damaging Deadlock
item.description: Romania is poised to break a months-long political impasse and get a new government that will be under pressure to retain investor confidence and avert a renewed economic crisis.
item.dc:creator: Andra Timu and Irina Vilcu

item.title: Trump Hints at Pulling Back Threat of US Bombardier Boycott
item.description: President Donald Trump indicated he would back away from threats to boycott Canadian firm Bombardier Inc., citing the company’s workforce in Kansas, as he campaigned in the state ahead of November’s midterm election.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: US Studies Centre’s Channer on Geopolitics
item.description: Hayley Channer, Economic Security Program Director at US Studies Centre, discusses the outlook for the US midterm elections and Australia’s strategic autonomy. She speaks with Haidi Stroud-Watts on the sidelines of the Citi ANZ Investment Conference in Sydney. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hegseth Meets Netanyahu in Israel, Days Before Vote, Axios Says
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a trip to the Middle East, just days before the country holds elections, Axios reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and John Harney

item.title: Seoul Vows to Boost DMZ Control After North Korea’s Threat
item.description: South Korea vowed to step up military operations to strengthen its control over the heavily fortified Demilitarized Zone that divides the peninsula, after Pyongyang warned it could deploy more strike assets to the border area.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Trump Uses Slur to Defend GOP Senator in Combative Speech
item.description: President Donald Trump used an antisemitic term during a rally in Kansas as he came to the defense of Republican Senator Roger Marshall, who faces a surprisingly competitive race in a deeply red state.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Kate Sullivan

item.title: Trump Open to Putin-Xi Talks Without Zelenskyy, Early Voting Underway for Majority of US
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) discusses the midterm elections and President Donald Trump's changing posture toward Russia as he seeks to increase Russian diesel exports, and Jane Harman, former democratic congresswoman from California, talks about the US relationship with Russia and China as well as the Trump's approach to Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Harman: US Foreign Policy in 'Freefall'
item.description: Jane Harman, former California democratic congresswoman, says US foreign and security policy is “in freefall” and argues the country lacks a strategy for Ukraine or the Middle East. Harman says Russian President Vladimir Putin is taking advantage of Trump and that Chinese President Xi Jinping has been “playing the long ball” successfully. She also says Congress needs to reassert its policymaking role, saying “Congress always chickens out.” She speaks with Kailey Leinz & Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Malliotakis Sees Diesel Prices in Trump’s Russia Shift
item.description: Rep. Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) says there is a lot of confusion over President Donald Trump’s changing posture toward Russia as Russian attacks on Ukraine continue. Malliotakis says Trump is focused on bringing down diesel prices and believes getting Russia to increase diesel exports is a major part of that effort. She also says Americans connect the Iran conflict to higher energy prices. She speaks with Kailey Leinz & Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Tech Earnings Kick Off
item.description:
A rebound in chipmakers buoyed the stock market Monday as dip buyers emerged on bets the artificial-intelligence investment boom will continue to support solid earnings. The advance in tech stocks lost steam last week as investors questioned the sustainability of AI spending, given the outlook for higher rates. This week’s earnings from Meta Platforms will provide a fresh proving ground for confidence in the AI trade, while SpaceX, Tesla, and Meta are also due to report. The industry is still set to account for nearly 70% of global earnings growth next year, according to Citigroup.
On today's episode:
Mandeep Singh, Bloomberg Intelligence Global Head of Technology Dan Ives, Partner at Yorkville Ives & Co. Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas & Ed Ludlow, Host of Bloomberg Tech Sophie Alexander, Bloomberg New Wealth Reporter & Alex Rajbhandari, Bloomberg News US Insurance Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Stocks Rebound as Investors Reassess the AI Trade
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Goldman Sachs Chief Credit Strategist Amanda Lynam, Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller, Jefferies Senior Equity Research Analyst, Airlines, A&D Sector Sheila Kahyaoglu, X-Energy CEO Clay Sell, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Meredith Whitney Advisory Group CEO Meredith Whitney, Alger Portfolio Manager Ankur Crawford, Espa Labs CEO & Co-Founder Deon Nicholas, JPMorgan Asset Management Chief Global Strategist David Kelly & JPMorgan Private Bank Global Investment Strategy Co-CIO Stephen Parker, & SIFMA CEO Ken Bentsen. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Trump Is Pushing Ukraine to Yield
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Donald Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia, escalating a weeklong row with the US president. We examine the rift between Kyiv and Washington with Bloomberg Opinion's Marc Champion. French officials have rolled out tougher security measures and pledged aid for businesses after cost-of-living protests this weekend devolved into violence and looting. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook has the latest from Paris. Perplexity CEO Aravind Srivinas and Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow discuss AI agents' role in financial services. Bloomberg's Brody Ford & Bailey Lipschultz look at why Nscale is facing pushback to its $30 billion IPO valuation target, with some investors suggesting $16 to $19 billion instead. Plus - US Energy Secretary Chris Wright speaks with Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern about energy security in the AI age. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: X-Energy CEO on Amazon, AEP Nuclear Data Center Deal
item.description: Amazon and American Electric Power are evaluating plans for a 960-megawatt nuclear plant in Indiana using 12 small reactors designed by X-Energy. X-Energy CEO Clay Sell says the companies have held substantial discussions for several months, and AEP has begun early site work and community engagement. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Virginia Wants 6-Year Rate Freeze in NextEra-Dominion Deal
item.description: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger won’t support NextEra Energy Inc.’s $67 billion Dominion Energy Inc. takeover without a six-year freeze on residential power rates, raising the bar for a utility mega-deal that’s facing increasing skepticism.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chediak

item.title: French Unrest Tapers Off After Security Measures Imposed
item.description: French protests largely died down after authorities rolled out tougher security measures, including targeted curfews, following cost-of-living protests over the weekend that degenerated into violence, vandalism and looting.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot

item.title: Ukraine Suspects US Blocking Intelligence on Russian Attacks
item.description: Ukrainian officials say they suspect the US is intermittently restricting intelligence sharing despite Trump administration denials, allowing Russian projectiles to strike Ukraine without warning — including in a ballistic missile attack on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Drozdiak, Courtney McBride and Daryna Krasnolutska

item.title: China Says Advanced Nuclear Sub Was Used to Test-Fire ICBM
item.description: China said it used its most advanced nuclear submarines to test-fire an intercontinental ballistic missile in the Pacific earlier this year, underscoring Beijing’s progress in the key defense technology.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao
